treatments.name: Lower blood pressure target (135/85 mm Hg or lower)
treatments.population: Adults with chronic arterial hypertension (mean age 63; mainly older people with moderate to high cardiovascular risk)
treatments.summary: Lower targets do not reduce total mortality or total serious adverse events compared with a standard target of 140/90 mm Hg or lower; benefits do not outweigh harms.

evidence.quote: Lower targets do not reduce total mortality (risk ratio (RR) 0.95, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.05; 11 trials, 38,688 participants; high-certainty evidence) and do not reduce total serious adverse events (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.99 to 1.08; 6 trials, 18,165 participants; moderate-certainty evidence).
evidence.statement: Lower targets did not reduce total mortality or total serious adverse events.

evidence.quote: For the general population of persons with elevated blood pressure, the benefits of trying to achieve a lower blood pressure target rather than a standard target (≤ 140/90 mm Hg) do not outweigh the harms associated with that intervention.
evidence.statement: For the general population, the benefits of a lower target do not outweigh the harms compared with ≤140/90 mm Hg.

evidence.quote: The results of this review are primarily applicable to older people with moderate to high cardiovascular risk.
evidence.statement: Findings apply mainly to older people with moderate to high cardiovascular risk.
